name: The Long Provision
description: One of the earliest and most technically accomplished corporate propaganda films of the modern era, commissioned by the Axiom Group to commemorate their 50th year of Meridian operations — a sweeping holographic historical drama depicting Axiom's infrastructure investments as acts of civic salvation, with a cast of 200 and a score performed by the Meridian Philharmonic. The film presents the Tier system as a natural meritocratic gradient rather than a designed architecture, and its depiction of Shelf communities as grateful recipients of Axiom services was considered standard framing at the time of release.
cultural_impact: The film's title became so thoroughly ironic in M88 political culture that 'a long provision' now universally means a promise designed to sound generous while ensuring permanent dependency — the phrase appears in protest art, mesh broadcasts, and runner slang alike.
story_hooks: The original director of The Long Provision left detailed private journals before his death describing what Axiom executives demanded be changed from his initial script — and his estate has just made them available to anyone who can get to them before Axiom does.

A current Axiom board member appears as a child extra in a background scene of The Long Provision — in a neighborhood the official record says they've never lived in, in a district that Axiom's own history says wasn't developed until a decade later.

Someone is distributing a version of The Long Provision with an entirely different third act replacing Axiom's triumphant legacy with archival footage of the communities displaced to build it — the edit is technically flawless and no one knows who made it.
